title: Hello, I'm new to RPG Maker , where does an initiate like me start?

posts.author: osirian87
posts.body: Hello, I'm new and I discovered rpg maker through several games made in it, for example fear of hungry, but when I discovered it I saw that I didn't know some things, for example javascript and most importantly, having a version of rpg maker xp, vx or maybe mv and among other things, if you can help me with something, maybe some advice or a tutorial, please be honest.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
Welcome! I'm confused by your question.
You discovered RPG Maker, you want to know where to start, but you didn't buy one yet?
I think that's pretty obviously the place to start. No tutorial means anything if you don't have the software to follow along and learn from.
It makes the most sense to get MZ, as it's the newest version with the nicest editor. MV is almost as good, especially if MZ is expensive for you or you prefer to have a larger assortment of plugins available. (MZ has lots of plugins, but there's still stuff for MV that hasn't been replicated, and the MV stuff is generally cheaper)
I don't think it makes much sense to start by getting an older version than that. You get more limited in what you can add to the game via scripts rather than the JavaScript plugins that MV and MZ support, and the software itself is more dated to the point of having compatibility issues on some systems.
Once you get RPG Maker, there's a tutorial built into it, as well as lots of YouTube channels with additional ones to follow along with.

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
Welcome to the forum!
If you haven’t bought a version yet, you could always download the 20-day trial version and recreate some tutorials to learn the basics.
Learning to really use the engine takes time, patience, and effort. But it can be very rewarding.
Good luck!

posts.author: VOCALKENNI
posts.body:
First of all: download a version of RPGmaker, secondly: delete RPGmaker [just kidding :3]
If you just wanna see if it's something you'd like I'd suggest getting the trial. It's pretty simple and easy to use. There are many very great tutorials on youtube if you need them [I personally used Toasty Time's tuts, he's great :3]
RPGmaker is great for creating your own story into a video game, the community is great and very helpful! It's a great way to get creative, and really challenge yourself.
Plugins are also very helpful if you need to add something into your game but don't know JS or any other coding method. Most plugins come with tutorials built into them :3
If you need help with anything that you're trying to do the forums are really great for that! :3
Edit: I haven't personally used any other version, but MZ has been really good for me :3

utunnels said:

Click to expand...
That's because with bundles you don't pay for the products you already have - it will be more expensive if you log out and then look at it.
This does mean that those bundles are effectively an additional discount to buy one of those programs if you already have the other, but that won't help someone who has neither (I'm not sure why you'd want to buy both straightaway).
